# Reproducibility Stress Test {.unnumbered}

## Goal

Students test whether a project can run in a fresh environment and document every failure before final submission.

## Fresh Environment Protocol

Complete these steps in a new Codespace or equivalent clean environment.

1. Open the repository from GitHub.
2. Locate the project README and follow only the documented setup steps.
3. Render the Quarto book or report.
4. Run the NHANES dashboard from the repository root.
5. Open the Week 11 static dashboard source and render it as a standalone Quarto dashboard.
6. Check that all data paths are relative.
7. Record every failure, warning, unclear instruction, and repair.
8. Commit repairs with clear messages.

## Failure Log

| Check | Result | Fix made | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository opens in fresh environment |  |  |  |
| Packages install or load |  |  |  |
| Report renders |  |  |  |
| Dashboard runs locally |  |  |  |
| Static dashboard renders |  |  |  |
| README instructions are accurate |  |  |  |
| Relative paths work |  |  |  |

## Peer Review Roles

- **Driver:** Runs the project exactly as documented.
- **Navigator:** Reads instructions aloud and logs ambiguity.
- **Auditor:** Checks paths, data provenance, citations, and AI-use notes.

Rotate roles after the first major failure or after 20 minutes.

## Final Repair Checklist

- [ ] All required outputs render or run from a fresh environment.
- [ ] README instructions match the actual workflow.
- [ ] Data paths are relative.
- [ ] Cached data files needed for offline work are present.
- [ ] Citations resolve.
- [ ] AI-use notes identify what was drafted and how it was checked.
- [ ] Remaining risks are documented in the failure log.
